title: Backup and Recovery

header.html: Create a Recovery Services vault; create an Azure Backup vault; create and configure a backup policy; perform backup and restore operations by using Azure Backup; configure Azure Site Recovery for Azure resources; perform a failover to a secondary region by using Site Recovery; configure and interpret reports and alerts for backups
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1Two vaults

Vault Protects (examples)
Recovery Services vault Azure VMs, files and folders (MARS agent), SQL Server in VMs, SAP HANA, Azure Files; also hosts Site Recovery
Backup vault Newer workloads: Azure Blobs, Azure Disks, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Kubernetes [Verify live]

The vault must be in the same region as the VMs it protects. Storage redundancy of the vault (LRS, ZRS, GRS) is chosen before protecting items; GRS with cross-region restore lets you restore in the paired region.

Exam tip

. "Back up an Azure VM" = a Recovery Services vault in the VM's region.

2Backup policies

A backup policy sets when to back up and how long to keep each backup.

Setting Fact
Schedule Daily or weekly, at a time you choose (some workloads more often)
Retention Daily, weekly, monthly, yearly retention points
Instant restore Snapshots kept locally (1 to 5 days) for fast restore
Soft delete Deleted backup data is kept 14 days by default and can be recovered

3Backup and restore operations

Operation Fact
Enable backup Choose the vault, the policy and the VM(s); the first backup is full, later ones incremental
Backup now On-demand backup
Restore a VM Create new VM, Replace existing, or Restore disks (then build the VM from them)
File recovery Mount the recovery point and copy files without restoring the whole VM
Stop protection Retain data (stop and keep) or delete it

4Azure Site Recovery (ASR)

Site Recovery gives disaster recovery: it replicates VMs to a secondary region so you can fail over during an outage.

Concept Meaning
Replication Continuous replication of VM disks to the target region
Recovery plan Ordered group of VMs with steps and scripts for failover
Test failover Validate the plan in an isolated network with no impact on production
Failover Switch to the replica VMs in the secondary region
Commit Finalize the failover (the recovery point is the one used)
Reprotect Reverse replication from the secondary back toward the primary
Failback Return to the original region

Exam tip

. Backup = restore data from a point in time. Site Recovery = keep a running replica in another region for failover. They are different and often used together.

5Reports and alerts

Tool Use
Backup reports Dashboards from Log Analytics data: usage, jobs, policies
Backup alerts Built-in alerts for failed jobs and other events; route to email or action groups
Azure Monitor Combine with metrics and alert rules
Exam tip

. A Recovery Services vault must be in the same region as the VMs it protects.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team wants to back up several Azure VMs. What should be created first?

  • AA storage firewall that allows only the subnet of the virtual machines
  • BA budget that limits the monthly spending of the virtual machines
  • CA resource lock on each virtual machine in the resource group
  • DA Recovery Services vault in the VMs' region
Show the answer

Answer: D. VMs are protected by a Recovery Services vault in the same region.

S2A user deleted one file inside a VM. What is the fastest restore?

  • AReplacing the whole VM
  • BFailing over to another region
  • CRebuilding the VM
  • DFile recovery by mounting a recovery point
Show the answer

Answer: D. File recovery copies individual files from a recovery point.

S3A company wants VMs replicated to another region so it can fail over during an outage. Which service fits?

  • AAzure Backup alone
  • BAzure Site Recovery
  • CAzure Advisor
  • DAzure Policy
Show the answer

Answer: B. Site Recovery replicates VMs for regional disaster recovery.

S4How can the failover plan be validated without affecting production?

  • AA test failover in an isolated network
  • BA real failover during a quiet night for the production site
  • CDeleting the replica VM and re-enabling replication
  • DA resource lock on the replica VM in the secondary region
Show the answer

Answer: A. Test failover is non-disruptive.

S5An administrator deletes a backup by mistake. How long can soft delete keep the data by default?

  • A1 day
  • B365 days
  • C14 days
  • D0 days
Show the answer

Answer: C. Backup soft delete keeps data for 14 days by default.

S6Which vault protects Azure Blobs and Azure Disks?

  • ARecovery Services vault
  • BBackup vault
  • CKey Vault
  • DLog Analytics workspace
Show the answer

Answer: B. Backup vaults protect the newer workloads.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Which vault type hosts Site Recovery?

Show the answer

A Recovery Services vault.

R2What does a recovery plan do?

Show the answer

Groups VMs and orders their failover steps.

R3What does reprotect do?

Show the answer

Reverses replication after a failover.

R4Name the three VM restore options.

Show the answer

Create new VM, replace existing, restore disks.

R5What does instant restore use?

Show the answer

Locally kept snapshots.

R6Where do backup reports get their data?

Show the answer

A Log Analytics workspace.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Vaults Recovery Services (VMs, files, SQL, Files, ASR); Backup vault (Blobs, Disks, PostgreSQL)
Policy schedule, retention, instant restore, soft delete 14 days
Restore new VM, replace, disks, file recovery
Site Recovery replicate, recovery plan, test failover, failover, commit, reprotect, failback
Reports backup reports (Log Analytics), backup alerts
